reason: The cited passages discuss general HEA design (E1), Ti-Zn intermetallic effects on corrosion in Mg alloys (E2), Mg content influence on microstructure and corrosion (E3), and solid-solution/intermetallic formation in lightweight alloys (E4), but none provides specific evidence that thermal aging drives Mg segregation away from the matrix, that Ti concentrates in secondary phases, or that this directly yields a denser protective oxide and improved corrosion resistance relative to an as-cast baseline. The key mechanistic premises are therefore largely unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Thermal exposure coarsens and chemically segregates initially metastable intermetallic compounds in Mg-containing lightweight HEAs.
Mg segregates away from the solid-solution matrix while passivating elements (e.g., Ti) concentrate in secondary phases.
This segregation promotes formation of a denser, more protective oxide film during high-temperature oxidation.
The microstructural evolution shifts local electrochemical behavior, improving corrosion resistance relative to the as-cast state.
The cited evidence demonstrates these specific segregation, oxidation, and corrosion improvement mechanisms in Mg-containing lightweight HEAs.
